title: What Did You Think of It?

steps.html:
Two people walk round a festival of light and agree about almost everything, except the giant face projected onto a building and the fish in a phone box. Learning to disagree about a thing you both enjoyed is most of what a review is.

  • Hear how English gives an impression rather than a verdict
  • Say what you liked, what you did not, and why
  • Watch a documentary about a traditional craft
  • Write a review

steps.title: Packing a description into one sentence
steps.html:
Recycled from Lesson 29, and aimed now at a review.

A review has to say what a thing was and what you thought of it, usually at the same time. Relative clauses do that in one move: the projection onto the town hall, which was the highlight of the evening, lasted about four minutes.

Notice the pattern in the recording: What I particularly like is … This is a cleft sentence, and it is a relative clause in disguise. It puts the thing you want to emphasise at the end, where English puts the important word.

Compare: I like the contrast of old and new — neutral. What I particularly like is the contrast of old and new — the contrast is now the point of the sentence.

The same works for negatives: The only thing I'm not so keen on is the crowds. The structure builds in the concession — everything else was fine.

In writing, keep the comma rule. The installation which everybody photographs is in the market tells the reader which installation. The installation, which everybody photographs, is in the market assumes they already know, and adds a fact.

steps.title: Example bank.
steps.html:
Ten sentences from the recording and from a review built on it.

What I particularly like is the contrast of old and new.
Cleft: the contrast is the point.

The highlight for me was that building with the giant face.
Picks one above the rest.

The only thing I'm not so keen on is the crowds.
Concedes everything else.

I really like the way the buildings seem to come alive.
The way works like a relative.

the projection, which lasted about four minutes, was the best of it
Non-defining: adds a fact.

the installation which everybody photographs
Defining: tells you which one.

a building whose whole front was used as a screen
Whose for a thing.

the square, where it was worst, was almost impassable
Where in a non-defining clause.

It didn't really live up to what the reviews had promised.
What = the thing which.

the fish in a phone box, which I did not see the point of
Preposition at the end — normal in a review.

steps.title: Turning three flat sentences into one review sentence
steps.html:
1. The notes: There was a projection onto the town hall. It lasted four minutes. It was the best thing in the festival.
  2. Decide which fact is the main claim. It is the third one, so that becomes the main clause: The projection onto the town hall was the best thing in the festival.
  3. The length is extra information about something already identified, so it goes into a non-defining clause, with commas: The projection onto the town hall, which lasted about four minutes, was the best thing in the festival.
  4. Now emphasise it with a cleft: What I liked most was the projection onto the town hall, which lasted about four minutes.
  5. Check the comma rule: which lasted four minutes does not tell us which projection, so it must have commas. If there had been two projections, you would drop them.

steps.title: Write a review.
steps.sub: 160–190 words. Review an event, a place or a performance you have been to. Say what it was, what was best, what was not, and whether you would recommend it.
steps.placeholder: The … runs for … and we went on …
steps.html:
• Open by saying what it is and when you went.
  • Name the best thing with a cleft: <i>What I particularly liked was…</i>
  • Use a non-defining relative clause to add a fact about it.
  • Give one hedged negative, using <i>The only thing…</i> or <i>a bit… though</i>.
  • Close with a recommendation that includes one practical condition.

Useful language

  • What I particularly liked was …
  • The highlight for me was … , which …
  • I really liked the way …
  • The only thing I wasn't so keen on was …
  • I found it a bit … , though.
  • It didn't quite live up to what the reviews had promised.
  • It is well worth going, if you can get there …
steps.modelHtml:
The winter light festival, second weekend

The festival runs for ten days across the old town, and we went on the Saturday, which was probably a mistake.

What I particularly liked was the projection onto the town hall, which lasted about four minutes and repeated every quarter of an hour. Modern light and sound against a building that has been there for two hundred years is a contrast that does not get old. The highlight for me was the giant face on the north side of the square; when it began moving in time with the music, several people near me stopped talking altogether.

The only thing I wasn't so keen on was the crowds. By eight the main square was too packed for my liking, and the installation everybody had been told to see did not live up to what the reviews had promised.

It is well worth going. Go on a weekday, and go late.
